slides.title: What is an API?
slides.narration:
Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial.
It is on What is an API?
slides.image_prompt: Title slide: 'What is an API?' with a modern, clean design and a subtle AI-related graphic in the background.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
content: Explain the restaurant waiter analogy for APIs.
Identify the components of an API interaction.
Recognize the purpose of API keys and requests.
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to define what an API is.
You will explain the API waiter analogy.
You will identify API interaction components.
And you will recognize API key and request purposes.
slides.image_prompt: Learning objectives slide with bullet points clearly listed.

slides.title: System Requirements
content: Browser on a computer or mobile.
slides.narration:
Here I am using a browser.
It is on a computer or mobile.
slides.image_prompt: System Requirements slide showing a laptop and a mobile phone with a browser open.

slides.title: Prerequisites
content: No coding needed for this part.
slides.narration:
To follow this tutorial, you must be connected to the internet.
No coding is needed for this part.
slides.image_prompt: Prerequisites slide with icons for internet connection and 'no code' symbol.

slides.title: Understanding APIs
slides.narration:
Today, we will explore a core concept.
It is key to understanding AI.
It's called an API.
slides.image_prompt: Abstract graphic representing a foundational concept or a 'key' unlocking AI understanding.

slides.title: API: The Restaurant Waiter Analogy
slides.narration:
Let's use an analogy to understand APIs.
Imagine you are at a restaurant.
You want to order a hamburger.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a person sitting at a restaurant table, looking at a menu. A thought bubble shows a hamburger.

slides.title: You are the Application
slides.narration:
In this analogy, you are like an application.
Your goal is to get something done.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a person, labeled 'Your Application', with a thought bubble indicating a task or desire.

slides.title: The Kitchen is the AI Model
content: The kitchen is the complex AI model.
You don't go into the kitchen.
slides.narration:
The kitchen is like the complex AI model.
You don't go into the kitchen yourself.
It's too complicated.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a busy, complex kitchen with chefs, pots, and pans. Label it 'AI Model'.

slides.title: The Waiter is the API
content: You give your order (prompt) to the waiter (API).
The waiter takes it to the kitchen.
slides.narration:
Instead, you give your order to a waiter.
This waiter is your API.
You give your prompt to the API.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a person (Your Application) handing a menu (Prompt) to a smiling waiter (API).

slides.title: The AI's Response
content: The waiter brings it back to you.
slides.narration:
The kitchen prepares your food.
The waiter brings the finished dish back.
This is the AI's response.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of the waiter (API) bringing a finished hamburger (AI's Response) back to the person (Your Application).

slides.title: What an API Does
content: API stands for Application Programming Interface.
slides.narration:
An API is an Application Programming Interface.
It acts as a messenger.
It takes your request to the AI model.
Then, it brings back the AI's response.

slides.title: API Keys: Your Secret Password
content: An API Key is a secret password.
slides.narration:
To place an order, you need permission.
An API Key is like a secret password.
It's your unique ID card.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a key or a lock icon with 'API Key' written on it, suggesting a secret access.

slides.title: Keeping Your API Key Private
slides.narration:
It proves you can use the AI service.
Always keep your API key private.
Never share it with anyone.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a person safeguarding a key, with a 'private' or 'confidential' stamp. Emphasize privacy.

slides.title: Making an API Request
slides.narration:
Now, let's talk about a request.
A request is like placing your order.
You send your API key.
You also send your prompt to the AI service.
slides.image_prompt: Diagram showing an application sending 'API Key' and 'Prompt' to an API gateway.

slides.title: Summary
content: APIs connect your app to AI.
slides.narration:
We learned what an API is.
It connects your application to AI.
The waiter analogy helps us understand.
API keys give you access.
Requests send your instructions.
slides.image_prompt: Summary slide with key points listed, possibly using small icons for each point.
